summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for a severe headache, nausea, and vomiting, with a history of hypertension, asthma, and prior lung and breast cancer. She presented with markedly elevated blood pressure (206/99 mmHg), slurred speech, and fatigue, but no fever or focal neurological deficits. CT head and chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities. Her symptoms were attributed to hypertensive emergency, exacerbated by poor adherence to antihypertensive medications during an asthma flare. Blood pressure control with medication led to resolution of symptoms. She was stabilized on amlodipine in addition to her prior regimen of lisinopril, metoprolol, and valsartan. Her asthma management, including a prednisone taper and azithromycin, was continued with instructions to follow up with her allergist. She was discharged home in stable condition with improved mental status and no residual deficits.
